title: G7 Nations to Release 100 Million Barrels of Oil and Diesel
summary:
Leaders of the G7, a group of major economies, have agreed to release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel. A barrel is a unit used to measure oil. The goal is to ease supply problems that have made fuel prices rise sharply.

The G7 includes the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France. The European Union also takes part in its meetings. The group said the release will include a "substantial release" of diesel in the coming days.

Diesel is a fuel used by trucks, farms and many businesses. When diesel costs more, the price of food and other essentials can also go up. President Donald Trump had threatened to ban diesel exports from the U.S. That could have lowered prices for U.S. consumers before November's midterm elections, but it would have raised prices elsewhere.

After a meeting led by French President Emmanuel Macron, the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels within four months. The International Energy Agency, or IEA, will coordinate the effort. The plan includes a large diesel release within the first 20 days. G7 members also agreed not to place export restrictions on each other's energy products.

Macron said the action should help bring down prices for petroleum products, especially diesel. Trump later said an export ban was "never really on the table." The price of Brent crude oil, a global benchmark, briefly dropped below $100 a barrel but rose back to around $102. Before the U.S. and Israel invaded Iran, it was trading at around $73. Oil analyst Matt Smith said prices rose again after reports of renewed strikes between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis in Yemen.
why_it_matters: Fuel prices affect the cost of moving goods, so decisions about oil and diesel can reach what families pay for food and other essentials.
